reasons: Section 12.3 gives AbbVie (our side) an unconditional right to terminate 'for any or no reason' on 90 days' notice, in whole or country-by-country, with no early-termination fee — this meets the fallback (60–90 days' notice, no penalty) on its material terms.

Harpoon's termination rights are confined to our uncured material breach (12.2) and insolvency (12.4); it has no convenience right, which exceeds even the preferred position, so there is nothing to redline.

Shortfalls versus preferred (90 rather than 30 days' notice; no express pro-rata prepaid-fee refund) are minor sub-elements correctly noted in the rationale rather than flagged as deviations, and are of limited relevance in a milestone/royalty structure.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a phrasing artefact — the clause uses 'for any or no reason' instead of 'for convenience' — and does not undermine the substance.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline text was altered and no counterparty comment was proposed.
